alts.question: Explain why 7 × 11 × 13 + 13 is a composite number.
alts.model_answer:
7 × 11 × 13 + 13 = 13 × (7 × 11 + 1) = 13 × 78 = 13 × 2 × 3 × 13.
It has factors other than 1 and itself, so it is composite.

rubric.p: Concludes composite (has factors other than 1 and itself)

alts.label: A

questions.question: Half the perimeter of a rectangular garden is 36 m, and its length is 4 m more than its width. Find the dimensions of the garden.
questions.model_answer:
Let length = l, width = w. l + w = 36 and l − w = 4.
Adding: 2l = 40, so l = 20 m and w = 16 m.

questions.topic: Tangents at the ends of a diameter
questions.question: Prove that the tangents drawn at the ends of a diameter of a circle are parallel.
questions.model_answer:
Let AB be a diameter of a circle with centre O, and let PQ and RS be the tangents at A and B.
OA ⟂ PQ and OB ⟂ RS (radius ⟂ tangent), so ∠OAP = ∠OBS = 90°.
These are alternate angles made by the transversal AB with PQ and RS and they are equal, so PQ ∥ RS.

rubric.p: Radius ⟂ tangent at both ends (90° each)
Equal alternate angles, so the tangents are parallel

alts.topic: Find angles from two trigonometric values
alts.question: If sin(A + B) = 1 and cos(A − B) = 1, where 0° < A + B ≤ 90° and A ≥ B, find A and B.
alts.model_answer:
sin(A + B) = 1 gives A + B = 90°. cos(A − B) = 1 gives A − B = 0°.
So A = B = 45°.
alts.label: A

questions.question: A die is thrown once. Find the probability of getting (i) a number greater than 4 (ii) an even prime number.
questions.model_answer:
Six equally likely outcomes.
(i) 5 or 6: 2/6 = 1/3.
(ii) The only even prime is 2: 1/6.

questions.question: Given that √5 is irrational, prove that 3 + 2√5 is irrational.
questions.model_answer:
Assume 3 + 2√5 is rational: 3 + 2√5 = a/b, with a, b co-prime integers, b ≠ 0.
Then √5 = (a − 3b)/(2b).
The right side is rational because a, b are integers, so √5 would be rational. This contradicts the fact that √5 is irrational. Hence 3 + 2√5 is irrational.

questions.question: If α and β are the zeroes of x² − 4x + 3, find (i) α² + β² and (ii) a quadratic polynomial whose zeroes are 2α and 2β.
questions.model_answer:
α + β = 4, αβ = 3.
(i) α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ = 16 − 6 = 10.
(ii) Sum of new zeroes = 2(α + β) = 8, product = 4αβ = 12. Polynomial: x² − 8x + 12 (or any non-zero multiple).

alts.question: A(−2, −1), B(a, 0), C(4, b) and D(1, 2) are the vertices of a parallelogram ABCD. Find a and b.
alts.model_answer:
The diagonals AC and BD bisect each other, so their mid-points coincide.
(−2 + 4)/2 = (a + 1)/2 gives a = 1.
(−1 + b)/2 = (0 + 2)/2 gives b = 3.

rubric.p: Mid-point of AC = mid-point of BD

alts.label: B

questions.topic: Parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus
questions.question: Prove that a parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus.
questions.model_answer:
Let ABCD touch the circle at P, Q, R, S on AB, BC, CD, DA. Tangents from an external point are equal: AP = AS, BP = BQ, CR = CQ, DR = DS.
Adding: (AP + BP) + (CR + DR) = (AS + DS) + (BQ + CQ), so AB + CD = AD + BC.
In a parallelogram AB = CD and AD = BC, so 2AB = 2AD, AB = AD. All four sides are equal: ABCD is a rhombus.

rubric.p: Equal tangent lengths from each vertex
Uses opposite sides equal to get AB = AD, so rhombus

alts.question: Prove that (cosec θ − cot θ)² = (1 − cos θ)/(1 + cos θ).
alts.model_answer:
LHS = (1/sin θ − cos θ/sin θ)² = (1 − cos θ)²/sin²θ = (1 − cos θ)²/(1 − cos²θ)
= (1 − cos θ)²/[(1 − cos θ)(1 + cos θ)] = (1 − cos θ)/(1 + cos θ) = RHS.
alts.label: A

alts.question: Prove that (sin A − 2 sin³A)/(2 cos³A − cos A) = tan A.
alts.model_answer:
LHS = sin A(1 − 2 sin²A)/[cos A(2 cos²A − 1)].
1 − 2 sin²A = 1 − 2(1 − cos²A) = 2 cos²A − 1.
So LHS = sin A/cos A = tan A.

rubric.p: Takes sin A and cos A common

alts.label: B

alts.question: A motorboat whose speed in still water is 15 km/h goes 30 km upstream and returns downstream to the starting point. The upstream trip takes 1½ hours more than the downstream trip. Find the speed of the stream.
alts.model_answer:
Let the stream speed be s km/h. Upstream speed 15 − s, downstream 15 + s.
30/(15 − s) − 30/(15 + s) = 3/2.
30 × 2s × 2 = 3(225 − s²), so 120s = 675 − 3s², i.e. s² + 40s − 225 = 0.
(s + 45)(s − 5) = 0, so s = 5 (s cannot be negative). The stream flows at 5 km/h.

rubric.p: Upstream/downstream speeds and the time equation

alts.label: A

alts.question: The diagonal of a rectangular field is 16 m more than its shorter side, and the longer side is 14 m more than the shorter side. Find the sides of the field.
alts.model_answer:
Let the shorter side be x m. Longer side x + 14, diagonal x + 16.
By Pythagoras: (x + 16)² = x² + (x + 14)².
x² + 32x + 256 = 2x² + 28x + 196, so x² − 4x − 60 = 0, (x − 10)(x + 6) = 0.
x = 10 (not −6). Sides: 10 m and 24 m (diagonal 26 m).
alts.label: B

questions.question:
ABCD is a trapezium with AB ∥ DC. Its diagonals AC and BD meet at O.
(a) Prove that AO/BO = CO/DO.
(b) If AO = 3x − 1, BO = 2x + 1, CO = 5x − 3 and DO = 6x − 5, find x.
questions.model_answer:
(a) In ΔAOB and ΔCOD: ∠OAB = ∠OCD (alternate angles, AB ∥ DC) and ∠AOB = ∠COD (vertically opposite). So ΔAOB ~ ΔCOD (AA). Hence AO/CO = BO/DO, i.e. AO/BO = CO/DO.
(b) (3x − 1)/(2x + 1) = (5x − 3)/(6x − 5) gives 18x² − 21x + 5 = 10x² − x − 3, so 8x² − 20x + 8 = 0, i.e. 2x² − 5x + 2 = 0, (2x − 1)(x − 2) = 0.
x = ½ makes CO = −½ (impossible), so x = 2.

rubric.p: Equal alternate angles and vertically opposite angles
Sets up the equation in x

alts.topic: Surface area of a combined solid
alts.question: A vessel is a hollow hemisphere with a hollow cylinder mounted on it. The diameter is 21 cm and the total height of the vessel is 20.5 cm. Find its inner surface area (π = 22/7).
alts.model_answer:
r = 10.5 cm. Height of the cylinder h = 20.5 − 10.5 = 10 cm.
Inner surface area = CSA of hemisphere + CSA of cylinder = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2πr(r + h)
= 2 × 22/7 × 10.5 × 20.5 = 66 × 20.5 = 1353 cm².
alts.label: A

alts.topic: Surface area of a combined solid
alts.question: A capsule is a cylinder with a hemisphere at each end. Its total length is 19 cm and its diameter is 7 cm. Find its surface area (π = 22/7).
alts.model_answer:
r = 3.5 cm. Length of the cylinder h = 19 − 2 × 3.5 = 12 cm.
Surface area = 2πrh + 2 × 2πr² = 2 × 22/7 × 3.5 × 12 + 4 × 22/7 × 12.25 = 264 + 154 = 418 cm².
alts.label: B

questions.question: A person on the deck of a ship, 10 m above the water, sees the top of a cliff at an angle of elevation of 45° and the base of the cliff at an angle of depression of 30°. Find the distance of the cliff from the ship and the height of the cliff (√3 ≈ 1.73).
questions.model_answer:
Let d be the distance. Depression of the base: tan 30° = 10/d, so d = 10√3 m ≈ 17.3 m.
Elevation of the top: tan 45° = x/d, where x is the height of the cliff above eye level, so x = 10√3 m.
Height of cliff = 10 + 10√3 = 10(1 + √3) m ≈ 27.3 m.
